body:
Reported by the user: in the admin tab, deleting a user with no step-up password
entered does nothing, with no indication that the password is what's missing.

## What was actually wrong

Both clients DID set a message — but rendered it as the page-level error at the
very TOP of the screen, far above the user rows. Scrolled down among several
users you never see it, so a blocked action reads as "nothing happened".

Android was worse: the password check ran INSIDE deleteUser(), i.e. AFTER the
T-112 confirmation dialog. So you tapped Delete, confirmed "yes, delete this
user", and then silently nothing happened.

## Fix (both clients)

- The missing-password complaint now renders AT the password field ("Enter your
  password to reset or delete a user."), with the field in an error state — where
  the user must act, not at the top of a scrolling page. Applies to reset too.
- It clears as soon as a password is typed.
- Android checks the password BEFORE opening the delete confirmation (matching
  web), so the user is never asked to confirm a deletion that then can't run.
- Web also focuses the password field so the fix is one keystroke away.

The page-level error stays for genuine API/network failures.

Deliberately NOT disabling the buttons: a disabled control is another silent
"nothing happens" — an explicit message that names the missing input teaches what
to do.

Verified: web 152 passed (3 new AdminPage tests: delete blocked+explained, reset
blocked+explained, complaint clears on typing) + tsc + lint; android
testDebugUnitTest + lintDebug (new AdminViewModel test).
title: Admin: missing step-up password blocks delete/reset with no visible reason
